name: English: short passages
author: KeyHalo contributors
description: Original short passages written for KeyHalo: everyday life, making things, keyboards, travel, food and science.

texts.text: The first coffee of the morning tastes best when the house is still quiet and the screen is still dark.
A good keyboard disappears under your hands. You stop thinking about keys and start thinking in words.
Rain on a tin roof sounds louder at night, as if the dark gives every drop a little more room to land.
Every printer in the workshop has a personality. One is fast and messy, one is slow and perfect, and one only works on Tuesdays.
Light from the Sun takes a little over eight minutes to reach us, so every sunset is a picture of the recent past.
The train left on time, which surprised everyone on the platform, including the conductor.
Bread needs only flour, water, salt and patience. Most people have the first three and run out of the last one.
She labelled every cable in the drawer, and for one glorious week she could find anything she wanted.
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood, which makes them sound like characters from a very strange fairy tale.
The bug was not in the code he had just written. It was in the comment above it, which promised something the code never did.
Walking through a new city without a map is the fastest way to find the bakery the locals never mention.
Typing fast is mostly about not stopping. Slow, steady and accurate beats quick bursts followed by long pauses.
The soup was better on the second day, as if the vegetables had spent the night getting to know each other.
Honey found in ancient tombs was still safe to eat, because almost nothing can grow in something that sweet and dry.
He spent an hour tuning the lighting on his desk, then turned it off because it was distracting him from work.
The bus driver waved at every other bus on the route, a small club of people who know every pothole in town.
A backup you have never restored is just a hope stored on another disk.
Sound travels about four times faster in water than in air, which is why whales can hear each other across an ocean.
The garden looked empty in March. By June it was a jungle, and nobody remembered planting half of it.
Soldering is easy once you learn that the iron heats the joint, and the joint melts the solder, not the other way round.
Old maps are full of confident mistakes: rivers that never existed and islands that moved every few years.
Lemons make everything taste brighter. A little juice at the end can rescue a dish that tastes flat.
The meeting could have been an email, and the email could have been a short note on the fridge.
Lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun, but it lasts so briefly that the air around it explodes into thunder.
On long flights, time becomes a rumour. You eat breakfast twice and still arrive before you left.
A tidy desk is not a sign of a tidy mind. It just means the mess has been moved into a drawer.
Practise the hard letters slowly. Speed is just accuracy that has been repeated until it feels easy.
The cat ignored the expensive bed and slept in the cardboard box it arrived in.
Bamboo can grow almost a metre in a single day, fast enough that you could watch it if you had the patience.
Version one shipped with a typo on the splash screen. Version two fixed it and added three new ones.
The best street food stall in the market has no sign, a long queue and a cook who never looks up.
Your fingers remember shortcuts long after your mind forgets the menus they replaced.
Snow muffles a city so well that the loudest sound on the street becomes your own footsteps.
A switch rated for fifty million presses will probably outlive the cable, the case and the person who bought it.
Mountains look closer in clear air, which is why the last hour of a hike always seems to take twice as long.
